newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen extends gains on BOJ's operations.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen extends gains on BOJ's operations.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen continued to firm in late Tuesday trade after the Bank of Japan (BOJ) left more yen in the market during its daily monetary operations, dealers said.
"BOJ's operations drained 400 billion yen instead of 500 million yen. By leaving the surplus in the market, it indicates a strong intention to keep rates low," said a Japanese dealer.
The projected market surplus was about 510 billion yen, dealers said.
At 1140 GMT, December Euroyen was at 99.10 against its IMM close of 99.06. Turnover was moderately light around 10.880 lots.
December Euroyen is expected to remain lock within 99.02 to 99.10 this week, dealers said.
They said the long end of the Japanese yield curve was firm despite concerns of ample supplies, notably from the utilities.
The Japanese government bonds (JGB) futures ended firmer, with June up 0.09 ticks at 126.57.
However, volume was a dismal 214 lots as buyers were sidelined due to the supply concerns.
Support and resistance for June JGB were seen at 126.41 and 126.70 respectively.
Nagging fears about further rate hikes in the U.S. capped Eurodollar's upside potential, dealers said.
"Trading has been very thin because investors are worried Eurodollars will decline further. There is a fear of more (U.S.) rate hikes due to the strong U.S. economy," a dealer said.
June Eurodollar futures ended flat against its IMM close at 93.96.
Dealers said activity was further dampened ahead of the U.S. consumer price index scheduled for release later Tuesday.
